items.title: Is Carnival Stock Cheap, Or Is The Cash Already Spoken For?
items.summary: Carnival Corporation (CCL) threw off free cash worth 9.7% of its market value over the last twelve months, more than twice the 4.4% median for an S&P 500 company. A yield that high usually means a bargain or a business the market expects to shrink. Carnival is not that simple. The cash is real, and a large share of it belongs to its lenders.

items.title: Should You Buy Carnival Stock While Europe Sails Emptier?
items.summary: Carnival Corporation (CCL) trades near $22, down about 26% over the past year, while the S&P 500 gained close to 18%. The easy read on a cruise line that cheap is that demand finally cracked. It has not. Carnival lowered its 2026 yield outlook after the Middle East conflict hit its European sailings, and part of that cut was its own choice to protect price rather than fill cabins.

items.title: MGM Stock Slips 14% in 3 Months: Is the Pullback a Buying Opportunity?
items.summary: MGM's 13.9% three-month slide puts its growth plans in focus, but uneven Vegas demand, digital losses and heavy Osaka spending cloud the buy case.

items.title: Airlines, Cruises, Casinos: Are Things Actually Looking Up?
items.summary: Airlines, cruise lines, and casino stocks all navigated the same peak travel season and came out in completely different places. The reasons why reveal which trade actually has a durable tailwind and which is one bad quarter away from a real problem.
